title: Gradient Descent
visual_thesis: A model learns by repeatedly measuring local slope and taking small controlled downhill steps.
central_object: A dot moving on a single loss curve.
primary_transformation: Wild oversized movement becomes small repeated movement that settles near the minimum.

scenes.viewer_question: Why can a model fail even when it knows the downhill direction?
scenes.visual_object: one dot on a loss curve
scenes.motion: The dot jumps across the bottom when the step is too large.
scenes.meaning: Direction is not enough; step size controls whether learning behaves.
scenes.caption: A downhill step can still miss the bottom.

scenes.viewer_question: What does the gradient actually tell us?
scenes.visual_object: tangent arrow on the same curve
scenes.motion: A tangent appears at the current dot and points downhill.
scenes.meaning: The gradient is a local measurement, not a map of the whole valley.
scenes.caption: The gradient reads the slope right here.

scenes.visual_object: the same dot and a shorter arrow
scenes.motion: The dot takes one small controlled step.
scenes.meaning: Learning improves when movement is measured.
scenes.caption: A small step turns direction into progress.

scenes.visual_object: a trail of dots converging to the minimum
scenes.motion: Each new dot lands closer to the bottom.
scenes.meaning: The algorithm works by repeating one local correction.
scenes.caption: Repeat the correction and the dot settles.

scenes.visual_object: the same curve with a simple loop
scenes.motion: Measure, step, and repeat labels orbit the minimum.
scenes.meaning: Gradient descent is measured movement, not magic.
scenes.caption: Learning is measured movement repeated.
